item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I have a couple problems with this one. The first thing that made me raise an eyebrow was the use of the word "culprit" when describing the recovery of SCP-708 - a more scientific way of saying it would be to call SCP-708 the "cause" or the "source" of the incident. That's the only issue I have with tone, though. The other issue has been mentioned by others - the "driver must be killed to be removed" bit - but not only do I dislike it, it's also contradictory: Just before this detail about SCP-708 is described, the article specifically states that SCP-708 does not provide any restraints to the driver leaving other than the driver's unwillingness to do so. In order for lethal force to be the only means of removing the driver, SCP-708 must contribute some sort of preventative measures in addition to the driver just not wanting to stop.

My biggest problem, though, is that this is a "thing what makes you go nuts for no reason". I guess it might be an old article, but the "for no reason" bit is a turn-off even if this was the first SCP of its kind ever. There's nothing really interesting about this one. It induces a compulsion and enthusiasm because it's powered by human energy. Okay, and? It can't even really be used to do its job - it might as well be a truck or a construction crane. Maybe I'm being exceptionally harsh tonight, but this won't suffer terribly from one person's disapproval anyway. Downvoted.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I really like this one, especially the bit about "and upon starting the vehicle, attempted to lift the transport, instead."

What I really don't like, as others have commented, is the "operator must be killed to remove them" bit. I just don't buy it. Tranquilizer darts don't work? Sure, I can allow that. But to say that there is exhaustively NOTHING that can remove the driver without killing them seems too far-fetched. Have they tried sleeping gas? Does the driver of SCP-708 not need to breathe? What if you got a sword and just cleaved the wrists off, could they be removed then? Or does SCP-708 actually grant invulnerability somehow?

I'd like to upvote this but will refrain from voting instead.

EDIT: And now that I think about it, is SCP-708 itself invulnerable? Can it be tipped over? That's one of the things they teach you immediately in forklift training - they can tip over more easily than you think.

I think I'm seeing a contradiction here…

In the second paragraph of the description it says (my emphasis) "If a subject is already engaged in operating SCP-708, those that were previously compelled to operate it, and those that maintain visual contact with the object, report a feeling of jealousy, wishing to remove the current operator."

Later it says that termination is the only way to remove the driver. So surely there wouldn't be anybody who has previously been compelled to operate it. Unless it means anybody who has previously felt the compulsion, whether or not they were allowed to go through with it?

item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded:
Good catch, he didn't actually say they were removed from the vehicle before they became fatigued.
I suppose if they held the vehicle in containment with a subject, it would probably keep them awake and fighting, until the fatigue caused them to colapse. Killing them. Still, seems like you could recover them once fatigue caused the muscles to fail from the abuse. It never says it gives them super human ability. For reduced risk to personel, I suggest using patients from ward 32. Yes, I know that's a children's ward. What? It should reduce maximum resistance to removal, even with adrenal boosting. Failing that, there is the amputation of limbs. Fewer limbs should result in less ability to resist. Mind you, use terminal subjects only, we're on a budget.
